headline: Touchscreen MacBook Pro coming next year, report says
summary: A new report suggests Apple is planning to introduce a touchscreen to its MacBook Pro lineup, potentially arriving in 2025.
details: Rumors suggest Apple is exploring the integration of touchscreens into its MacBook Pro models.
This potential move, if it materializes, could see the first touchscreen MacBooks arrive as early as 2025.
While Apple has historically resisted adding touchscreens to its laptops, citing usability concerns, this report indicates a shift in strategy.
The company has been refining its ProMotion display technology and exploring new user interface paradigms, which could pave the way for this feature.
caption:
Apple's MacBook Pro could finally be getting a touchscreen.

headline_marked: [[ASUS monitor]] blocks bullet fired through wall during Call of Duty session
headline: ASUS monitor blocks bullet fired through wall during Call of Duty session
summary: A gamer is calling their $280 ASUS TUF monitor 'the best $280 I ever spent' after it stopped a bullet that passed through their wall, narrowly missing them.
details: A Reddit user shared an astonishing story of their ASUS TUF VG258QM 280Hz gaming monitor saving them from a bullet. The projectile, fired through the wall of their home, struck the monitor while they were playing Call of Duty, preventing serious injury.

While monitors are not designed for ballistic protection, the plastic casing and internal components of this ASUS TUF display were sufficient to stop the bullet after it had already penetrated the exterior wall. The user humorously declared it 'the best $280 I ever spent'.

ASUS has acknowledged the incident and stated they will investigate. While the monitor sustained damage, it reportedly still functions aside from the impacted area, making for an unexpected advertisement for the TUF (The Ultimate Force) branding, known for its durability and adherence to MIL-STD-810H testing protocols.

This is not the first time gaming hardware has unexpectedly stopped bullets; similar incidents involving a gaming PC and a Razer headset have been reported previously. The user mentioned they were already considering a new display, making this a convenient, albeit dramatic, catalyst for an upgrade.
